title: Flock camera paranoia handcuffs the police | Mike Rosen - Denver Gazette
summary: Denver Gazette columnist Mike Rosen defends Flock Safety's ALPR cameras as valuable crime-fighting tools, dismissing privacy and Fourth Amendment concerns as paranoia. He criticizes sanctuary-city activists who oppose sharing Flock data with ICE.

key_quotes.quote: Flock's automated license plate readers, installed at intersections all over town with the consent of local governments across the country, photograph the plate and record details, including GPS locations, of every passing vehicle and compare the data to a "hot list" stored in the Flock system of all wanted plates nationwide.
A large element of those who oppose Flock cameras are sanctuary-city activists who want open borders... They don't want data from those cameras to be shared with federal authorities like ICE

It was a Flock camera in Boulder that quickly located the car and aided police in the arrest and conviction for murder of the Islamist antisemitic terrorist who firebombed a crowd on the Pearl Street Mall.
